parties:
Tapan Nath -------- Petitioner.
Vs.
Bibha Nath -------- Respondents.
full_judgment:
Amirul Islam Chowdhury, J.—This matter has come before us, under section 17, of the Divorce Act, (hereinafter referred to as the Act) for confirmation of the decree for dissolution of the marriage of the parties made by the District Judge, Khulna on 31st August, 1979 in Title Suit No. 3 of 1978. 

 3. It appears from the records that as application under section 10 of the Act has been filed by petitioner Tapaa Nath on 18.1.78 alleging therein that petitioner Tapan Nath married respondent Bibha Nath on 18-2-65 in accordance with Christian Law of marriage and they lived as husband and wife and had three children out of their wedlock. That respondent Bibba Nath become disloyal to petitioner Tapan Nath and had free mixing with their neighbors James, Harendra Nath, titling and Samir and committed acts of adultery with them. As such petitioner Tapan Nath prayed for a decree for dissolution of his marriage with respondent Bibha Nath. Respondent Bibha Nath entered appearance and filed a written statement denying the allegation of adultery as contained in paragraph 3 of the petition. Respondent Bibha Nath, however, did not appear at the time of hearing of the suit and the suit was beard and decreed expire. 

 7. Accordingly, we set aside the decree dissolving the marriage of the petitioner and the respondent and order a retrial of the petition in accordance with the provisions of the Act. The trial court should call upon the petitioner to give further and better particulars as to his allegation of adultery contained in paragraph 3 of the petition. The learned District Judge may give opportunity to the petitioner to amend his petition if be so desires. The learned District Judge may also afford lawful opportunity to the respondent to amend her written statement if she no desires. The learned Distract Judge is further directed to frame appropriate issues in the light of the pleadings of the parties and on conclusion of the trial to give his findings on the issues.
